question.text: Per the PDF, apart from methodology change, which of the following is NOT among the major contributors to change in the value of an investee company in a Cat II AIF's portfolio?

answer.text: Quarterly sentiment surveys of retail equity investors
Changes in external environment and market variables
Changes in business performance of the investee company
Changes in the tax environment affecting the investee

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PDF Section 11.8, the five contributors are: (1) external environment / market variables, (2) investee business performance, (3) tax environment, (4) capital structure changes, (5) valuation methodology changes. Retail sentiment surveys are not a listed driver — retail sentiment affects listed stocks but not private-market fair-value estimates. **The Trap:** All other three options are explicit drivers from the PDF. Retail sentiment is a listed-market phenomenon and is not in the IPEV/PDF-listed driver set for unlisted portfolio marks. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same drivers. XXI-B (PM) deals with listed where retail sentiment matters. For Cat I/II private positions, sentiment is irrelevant — fundamentals dominate. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Track the five drivers in your quarterly investee update: market, performance, tax, capital structure, methodology. This five-heading template works well for LP letters — LPs can quickly parse what drove NAV changes.
